_note: Every handling number in one place. Mass is in tonnes and thrust in kN, so thrust / mass is m/s². Speeds are m/s, angles degrees, times seconds.

planet.name: Ochre IV
planet._note: Above the ceiling (metres of altitude) the ship flies on space handling: no weight and the space top speed.

turning._note: Turn rate in °/s is total gyro torque / mass, never below the floor. Roll is rollFactor times faster. spinUpTime is how long it takes to reach full turn rate.

assist._note: Flight assist brakes with the thrusters facing the right way, never weaker than minBrake (m/s²). The last part of every change eases out at easeRate (1/s), so stops are smooth. cruiseRate is how fast W/S change the cruise speed (m/s per s). horizonLevel (1/s) eases the wings back to level in air when you aren't rolling, so a first ship is forgiving; 0 turns it off.

hover._note: The ride-height spring: verticalGain (1/s) closes the height error, limited to maxRise up and maxGrip down (m/s²); grip only holds within gripBand metres above ride height, so jumps fly. Look-ahead probes reach speed * lookAheadTime ahead (clamped); terrain ahead that rises more than stepAllowance * ride height lifts the vessel early. levelRate (1/s) settles tilt. Slopes steeper than maxSlope (°) are refused. Probes reach probeDepth * ride height below the engines.

gear._note: Gear drops by itself below deployAltitude (m above ground) when slower than deploySpeed, and comes up again past them plus hysteresis. A ship on its gear, slower than landSpeed, with nobody touching the controls for idleBeforeLanding, settles over settleTime and stops simulating.

contacts._note: Damage = mass * (impact speed - safeSpeed)² * damageScale, where mass is the vessel's for ground hits and the reduced mass m1*m2/(m1+m2) for ramming (both sides take it). Hull points = hull mass * hullPointsPerTonne. Contacts bounce off with restitution and lose scrape of their sliding speed only when they do damage. Ground hits faster than craterSpeed blast a crater of craterScale * cbrt(energy in MJ) metres, never wider than craterMaxRadius.
